cards.text: Isaiah the prophet has had hard news for God's people. They ran to Egypt for help without asking the LORD, and when He told them repentance and rest would save them, they said no thanks, we'll flee on horses (Isaiah 30:2, 15-16). So when the prophet says "Therefore," friend, I'd be hiding behind my own mustache.

cards.question: After all that running and refusing, the prophet says "Therefore." What does the LORD long to do for His people?

cards.text: He rises to show them compassion, for the LORD is a just God. Remember, these are the folks who'd rather ride off on horses than rest and trust Him (Isaiah 30:15-16).

cards.question: The prophet says, "Blessed are all who ___ for Him."

cards.text: Then the prophet speaks straight to the people in Zion who dwell in Jerusalem: "you will weep no more." Friend, I cried in that junk drawer so long the dust started handing me tissues.

cards.question: When the people in Jerusalem cry for help, the LORD hears them but stays silent.

cards.text: Now, hard days still come: the Lord will give them the bread of adversity and the water of affliction. That's one delivery NOBODY tips the driver for.

cards.question: Even in those hard days, something changes about the people's Teacher. What is it?

answers.text: He will no longer hide Himself
He will leave them on their own
He will only speak in dreams

cards.text: With their own eyes they'll see Him. And whether they turn to the right or to the left, their ears will hear a command.

cards.question: Whether they turn right or left, the people will hear the command ___ them.

cards.text: And the command is, "This is the way. Walk in it." A voice that steers you right BEFORE you're three exits past it? Friend, that beats every map app on earth.

cards.question: Now God's people are walking His way. What do they do with their silver-plated idols and gold-plated images?

cards.text: They desecrate those idols, toss them out and tell them, "Be gone!" Then the prophet turns to the seed they've sown in the ground.

cards.question: The LORD will send ___ for the seed they have sown in the ground.
Even after the LORD sends for their seed, the food from their land stays thin and scarce.

cards.text: Their cattle graze in open pastures, and the oxen and donkeys eat salted fodder, winnowed with shovel and pitchfork. Friend, those donkeys are eating fancier than I ever did in the drawer, and I lived on DUST.

cards.question: There's water coming too. Where will streams of water flow from?

answers.text: Every high mountain and raised hill

cards.text: Those streams flow in the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall. Then the sky joins in: the moon as bright as the sun, and the sun SEVEN times brighter.

cards.question: The moon shines like the sun, and the sun shines seven times brighter. On what day does that happen?

answers.text: When the LORD heals His people
When Egypt's army arrives to help
When Jerusalem's new wall is done

cards.text: Then the prophet says, "Behold," and the Name of the LORD comes from afar, with burning anger and dense smoke. His lips are full of fury, and His tongue is like a consuming fire.

cards.question: The LORD comes to sift His own people in a sieve of destruction.

cards.text: It's the nations He sifts, and His breath is like a rushing torrent that rises to the neck. He bridles the jaws of the peoples to lead them astray, like a horse with a bit that does NOT get to pick the road.

cards.question: Then the prophet turns back to God's people. What will they do?

answers.text: Sing as on a festival night

cards.text: Their hearts will rejoice like someone walking to the music of a flute, going up to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel. Picture your best commute ever, then delete the traffic.

cards.question: The LORD will make His majestic voice heard and reveal His mighty arm, striking in angry wrath. What comes with it?
At the voice of the LORD, ___ will be shattered.

cards.text: He will strike them with His scepter. And friend, this battle comes with a soundtrack.

cards.question: With every stroke of the LORD's rod on Assyria, tambourines and lyres will sound.

cards.text: Then the prophet names a place: Topheth. It has long been prepared, made ready for the king, and its funeral pyre is deep and wide, with plenty of fire and wood.

cards.question: Topheth's pyre is ready for the king. What sets it ablaze, like a torrent of burning sulfur?
